game: TEN @ CIN, Week 8 2026, pre-kick. CIN -13.5, total 46.5, implied CIN 30.0 / TEN 16.5. Weather snapshot wind 4.1 mph, temp 76.1 (no precip in pack).

script.base: Cincinnati should lead by halftime and again late. A 30-point Bengals total will not come from Chase Brown at 2.67 YPC in a committee with Samaje Perine (33 and 21 carries over the logged three games), so Joe Burrow builds the lead through Tee Higgins, who has 408 of 903 recent air yards. Tennessee, implied 16.5 as a 13.5 dog, falls behind and throws more; Tony Pollard's 19-carry pace is the volume that gets cut if the hole is two scores. Second half leans run-clock for Cincinnati, but not a first-quarter benching.
script.flip1: Tennessee hangs around because Cincinnati allows 4.88 YPC and Pollard keeps a full carry count. The game stays inside one score, both passing games play four quarters, and Higgins/Chase are not sat.
script.flip2: Cincinnati is up three scores early, Burrow and the wideouts are clock-killed or rested, favorite receiver yards stall, and Tennessee abandons the run so Pollard finishes well under his recent carry rate.

pre_mortem: Monday the Higgins over lost because Cincinnati led 24-3 at half, ran it with Brown and Perine, and Higgins finished on the 22-yard side of his last four after the defense took away the 408-air-yard shots. The Chase under lost the other way: he was the explosive they could not stop, one 20-plus play turned a 55-yard day into another 98, and fading the name on a three-game usage blip without an injury was the miss. If that explosive counter is the one that shows up, the Chase leg is the one that should have been dropped; the Higgins number at least matches who is getting the air yards.
slip_story: One story only: Cincinnati scores about 30 through Burrow, Higgins keeps the air-yard share and clears 72.5, and Chase's 83.5 is a stale alpha price that stays under in a two-score lead. Not a shootout stack, not a favorite clock-kill RB stack, and not mixed with a total under. Pollard is the dog-run piece of the opposite flip and stays off the slip. Max two legs; no TD, no receptions, no passing yards.
